title: Tamil Nadu Politics – Morning Brief – 3 November 2026
headline: Madras HC Grants Bail to DMK Leader, Citing Free Speech

top_developments.headline: Madras HC grants bail to DMK councillor in CM abuse case
top_developments.summary: The Madras High Court has granted anticipatory bail to Greater Chennai Corporation Ward 95 councillor D. Sudha, who faced police complaints for derogatory remarks against Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. Observing that no immediate complaint was filed for 12 days, the court remarked that a democratic government confident in its governance must meet public mockery with performance rather than rushing to make arrests.
top_developments.why_it_matters: The ruling sets a key legal precedent on how political criticism and state responses are handled under the current administration.

sources.title: Madras High Court grants relief to DMK councillor booked for remarks against CM Vijay

top_developments.headline: Stalin and opposition lambast TVK regime over sluggish GST growth
top_developments.summary: DMK president M.K. Stalin and opposition leaders, including AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami and BJP leader Annamalai, severely criticized the ruling TVK government over Tamil Nadu's meager 3% GST revenue growth in October. Leaders argued that the slowdown reflects economic mismanagement, industrial stagnation, and inflation higher than the national average. In response, Law Minister R. Nirmalkumar blamed the previous five years of industrial decline for the current fiscal lag.
top_developments.why_it_matters: Sluggish GST collections highlight mounting friction between the ruling party and opposition over state economic health.

sources.title: Edappadi K Palaniswami criticises Tamil Nadu government over price rise and GST loss

top_developments.headline: TNHB moves to raze Pattinapakkam flats amid Secretariat project buzz
top_developments.summary: Adding momentum to political speculation surrounding a new Legislative Assembly and Secretariat complex, the Tamil Nadu Housing Board has issued a tender to demolish 96 unsafe rental flats in Pattinapakkam. The state government previously granted in-principle approval to construct the new administrative hub on the land. The move has already triggered local political debate and environmental concerns over the massive proposed infrastructure project.
top_developments.why_it_matters: Clearing the Pattinapakkam site marks a concrete step toward realizing the government's controversial new Secretariat plan.

sources.title: Secretariat in making? TNHB to raze Pattinapakkam flats

sections.government_and_administration: - **CM Vijay Inaugurates Projects in Pudukkottai:** Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay visited Pudukkottai to distribute welfare assistance worth Rs 62.73 crore, inaugurate Rs 68.31 crore worth of completed works including a new bus stand, and lay foundations for fresh projects. Heavy crowds and frenzied fans tested police security and crowd-control measures during his maiden official tour to the district. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/cm-vijay-launches-rs-6831-cr-projects-takes-poll-like-roadshow-in-pudukkottai))
sections.political_parties_and_opposition: - **Five Arrested Over VCK Functionary's Murder:** Police arrested five suspects, including a local DMK functionary, within six hours of the murder of VCK worker Balamurugan in Ottapidaram. Investigators stated that the brutal killing stemmed from a local dispute regarding the placement of political flex banners along the Sottaiyan Thoppu main road. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/vck-mans-murder-dmk-cadre-among-5-held))
sections.assembly_courts_and_policy: - **CPM Opposes Traditional Attire Order:** The CPI(M) state executive committee has rejected Tamil Development Minister Rajmohan's proposal to mandate traditional office attire for state government employees one day a week. Party leaders stated the rule is completely inappropriate because regional traditional clothing varies widely, warning that it could trigger avoidable workplace disputes and cultural controversies. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/traditional-attire-order-flawed-says-cpm))
sections.district_developments: - **Thanjavur Farmers Protest Dropped Bridge Project:** Residents and farmers from over 40 villages in Thanjavur staged a public demonstration demanding the revival of the cancelled Rs 42-crore elevated bridge project across the Thenpermbur barrage. The protesters pointed out that abandoning the initiative forces commuters to take a lengthy 25-kilometer detour to reach nearby destinations daily. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/thanjavur-farmers-protest-dropping-of-bridge-project))
